items.stem: A dataset of incomes is strongly right-skewed. Which measure best represents a typical value?

options.rationale: Correct: the median resists the pull of extreme high values in a skewed distribution.
The mean is dragged upward by large outliers in a right-skewed distribution.
The maximum is an extreme, not a typical value.
The range measures spread, not a typical value.

items.explanation: Correct: for skewed data the median is a more representative centre than the mean.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about a 95% confidence interval for a mean are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: A larger sample size tends to narrow the interval
options.rationale: Correct: larger samples reduce the standard error, narrowing the interval.

options.text: It is built from the sample's standard error
options.rationale: Correct: the interval uses the standard error of the estimate.

options.text: It guarantees the true mean lies inside this specific interval
options.rationale: The 95% refers to the long-run procedure, not certainty for one interval.

options.text: It is the same as the standard deviation of the data
options.rationale: The interval and the data's standard deviation are different quantities.

items.explanation: Correct: a confidence interval is based on the standard error and narrows with larger samples.

items.stem: What does a p-value of 0.03 mean in a hypothesis test?

options.text: If the null hypothesis were true, data this extreme would occur about 3% of the time
options.rationale: Correct: the p-value is the probability of data at least this extreme assuming the null is true.

options.text: There is a 3% chance the null hypothesis is true
options.rationale: The p-value is not the probability that the null is true.
A p-value is not an effect size.
Statistical significance does not establish practical importance.

items.explanation: Correct: a p-value measures how surprising the data are if the null hypothesis holds.
